author: Claude
family_retired: movement/reachability-based bounds generally, at both granularities: Round 74 killed within-orbit segment capacity (a +1/+2 walk sweeps a 5-cycle), this round kills between-orbit sequencing (the generators make the space strongly connected with uniform out-degree 10-55). The engine's group action is too transitive for reachability arguments to obstruct anything.
global_status_unchanged: THIS PROJECT HAS NOT PROVED L6 >= 872 UNCONDITIONALLY.
lesson: every bound that has ever bitten in this project is a resource-counting bound (Phi, Ndef, O, dead ports, incidence excess r); never a reachability bound

near_miss_caught.corrected: adding E^1 collapses the graph to a single SCC on all 720 nodes
near_miss_caught.error: it OMITTED E^1 (ell=5, w2:10), which is also free; E^1 makes each orbit's five phases a directed 5-cycle
near_miss_caught.what: my first free-movement graph used only the ell=5 w3:201/210 edges and reported 15 SCCs, largest 48 -- which looks exactly like the obstruction being sought
near_miss_caught.why_it_matters: omitting a free move deletes legal transitions, inflating the crossing count and yielding an UNSOUND lower bound -- exactly the discipline the brief sets out (when uncertain, ADD edges rather than remove them). Had this graph been used it would have produced a second retraction.

payoff.stop_reason: condensation crossings are 0 for every state regardless of the corpus

scope: Q2 / Area-A. No search, no frontier re-run, no bounded continuation. Per-orbit segment-capacity family retired and not revisited.

sequencing_lower_bounds.note: every candidate form listed in the brief evaluates to zero; the condensation is a property of the generators, not of the corpus, so no residual sweep was needed

successor_scarcity_in_band.conclusion: blocking would require the open set to contain one specific 10-element successor set -- impossible at O < 10 -- and even then it forces a single paid move that ORBIT-REENTRY may already charge
successor_scarcity_in_band.residual_open_orbit_count: O in 3..10, so at least 134 of 144 orbits are still fresh

transition_digraph.cost_model: into an already-open orbit: (5-ell) units of Phi plus 1 unit of Ndef if weight 3 (an R). Into a fresh orbit the O is charged separately so only Phi remains; weight 2 into a fresh orbit is impossible (needs an abandonment -> F=2)
transition_digraph.reason: not one of the 7,920 transitions is available from all five source phases, so a 144-node orbit-only graph would assert movements the engine cannot make from the port actually occupied
transition_digraph.weakest_sound_refinement: (orbit, phase) -- 720 nodes, i.e. the permutations themselves

weakest_theorem_worth_proving_next.cheap_to_test: r = P - |T| is computable from the stored masks alone; whether the residual band sits at r = 0 or r = 1 decides the payoff
weakest_theorem_worth_proving_next.combined_with: Round 69: r is non-decreasing, and 6r <= 11 - Phi forces r <= 1 throughout the Q2 region
weakest_theorem_worth_proving_next.derivation: at an Area-A NR6 completion P = 121 and all 720 windows are visited, so all 120 hexagons are touched: |T| = 120, hence r_final = P - |T| = 121 - 120 = 1 EXACTLY
weakest_theorem_worth_proving_next.statement: a completion needs r to be exactly 1 at the end; a state with r = 1 must never create a second doubly-registered hexagon (already proved), and a state with r = 0 must still create exactly one -- which by Round 69's re-entry accounting requires re-entering a hexagon that already holds visited windows, costing Phi
weakest_theorem_worth_proving_next.why_it_survives_the_audits: it is a DEMAND-side charge on Phi that no current bound levies, and it survives q0 return and repeated re-entry because creating a bridge is a specific event, not a movement assumption
